title: Define what counts once
statement: Say what an answer accepts in one place, since rules written separately for the same answer drift apart.
example: One blank had three acceptance rules that disagreed, and another had four.
detail: Two external audits of five reading lessons found answers whose acceptance rules disagreed: two blanks each had three rules that disagreed, one had four, another's rubric and its synonym list disagreed, and a word bank keyed 'evil' as right while the same step's hunt left it off its accept list (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-30/REGISTER.md`; `grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-29/REGISTER.md`). The same audits found one sentence accepted as evidence on one page and rejected on another, in two lessons. Counting the same evidence the same way wherever it appears would carry this rule across pages, but that case still awaits a ruling.
against: Whether one sentence may count as evidence on one page and not on another is still waiting for a ruling (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-29/REGISTER.md`), and one audit filed that case as worth a look, not serious (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-inceptbench-2026-09-30/REGISTER.md`).
